domain_symbols.cad: computer-aided design parametric and geometric modeling
domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: Homogeneous 3D transform composition
preconditions: T1 and T2 are valid SE(3) homogeneous matrices
rules.operation: Compose two rigid 3D transforms by matrix product; not commutative in general.
examples: Rotate then translate is encoded as T_translate * T_rotate when transforming column points
counterexamples: Assuming T1 * T2 = T2 * T1 in general
common_errors: Mixing row-vector and column-vector multiplication conventions

rules.name: Rotation matrix orthonormality
rules.operation: Enforce orthonormal columns and unit determinant for valid rotations.
examples: Any rotation about an axis by angle theta satisfies R^T R = I
common_errors: Accumulated floating-point drift breaks orthonormality without re-orthogonalization

rules.name: Quaternion to rotation matrix
rules.input_form: unit quaternion q = (w, x, y, z)
rules.operation: Convert a unit quaternion to its equivalent rotation matrix to avoid gimbal lock and ease interpolation.
counterexamples: Non-unit quaternions induce scaling, not pure rotation
common_errors: Forgetting that q and -q represent the same rotation

rules.name: Bezier curve definition
rules.input_form: control points P_0..P_n, parameter t in [0,1]
rules.operation: Evaluate the Bernstein-basis polynomial Bezier curve at parameter t.
examples: A cubic Bezier (n=3) is the standard CAD curve primitive
counterexamples: Bezier curves do not in general pass through interior control points
common_errors: Using t outside [0,1] without explicit extrapolation semantics

rules.name: NURBS rational evaluation
rules.input_form: control points P_i with weights w_i and B-spline basis N_{i,p}(t)
rules.output_form: C(t) = sum_i N_{i,p}(t) w_i P_i / sum_i N_{i,p}(t) w_i
preconditions: weights w_i > 0 and valid knot vector
rules.operation: Evaluate a NURBS curve as a rational combination of weighted control points.
examples: A circle requires nonuniform weights and cannot be a polynomial Bezier
counterexamples: Zero or negative weights are not allowed in standard NURBS

rules.name: B-spline knot multiplicity continuity
rules.input_form: B-spline of degree p with knot of multiplicity k
rules.operation: Determine geometric continuity from knot multiplicity for B-spline curves and surfaces.
examples: A cubic B-spline with knot multiplicity 1 is C^2 at that knot
counterexamples: Multiplicity p+1 produces a discontinuity (curve break)
common_errors: Inserting full-multiplicity knots and expecting smoothness

rules.name: Boundary representation Euler-Poincare formula
rules.input_form: B-rep solid with V vertices, E edges, F faces, H holes-in-faces, S shells, G genus
rules.operation: Validate B-rep topological consistency via the generalized Euler-Poincare relation.
counterexamples: Open meshes violate the closed-shell precondition
common_errors: Forgetting to count interior face holes (H)

rules.name: CSG boolean union of solids
rules.input_form: solids A, B as point sets
rules.output_form: A union B with regularized boundary
preconditions: A and B are r-sets (regular closed point sets)
rules.operation: Compute the regularized union to ensure the result is again a valid solid (no dangling faces or edges).
examples: Union of two overlapping cubes yields a single solid
counterexamples: Unregularized union may leave coincident faces

rules.name: Parametric constraint Jacobian rank
rules.input_form: constraint system f(x) = 0 with Jacobian J(x)
preconditions: f is C^1 and J defined at x
rules.operation: Compute remaining degrees of freedom of a 2D/3D sketch from constraint Jacobian rank.
examples: A fully constrained 2D sketch has rank(J) = n
counterexamples: Redundant constraints reduce rank without reducing DOF further
common_errors: Confusing overconstrained inconsistent systems with overconstrained consistent ones

rules.name: Surface of revolution
rules.input_form: profile curve r(u) revolved about axis a by angle v in [0, 2*pi]
preconditions: profile lies in plane containing axis
rules.operation: Construct a parametric revolved surface by rotating a profile curve about an axis.
examples: A line offset from the z-axis generates a cylinder
counterexamples: A profile crossing the axis creates self-intersections
common_errors: Allowing profile self-intersection produces an invalid surface

rules.name: Mesh decimation quadric error metric
rules.input_form: vertex v with associated 4x4 quadric Q_v
rules.output_form: edge collapse cost = v^T Q v
preconditions: Q_v is sum of plane quadrics from incident faces
rules.operation: Use the Garland-Heckbert quadric error metric to prioritize edge collapses during mesh simplification.
examples: Planar regions collapse first because their error is near zero
counterexamples: Ignoring boundary edges loses silhouette features
common_errors: Not protecting feature edges from collapse

rules.name: STEP AP242 PDQ minimum tolerance
rules.input_form: geometric model exported to STEP AP242
rules.output_form: shape tolerance fields populated with PDQ-compliant values
preconditions: Model passes Product Data Quality (PDQ) shape checks
rules.operation: Encode product manufacturing information and tolerances in ISO 10303-242 to ensure downstream interoperability.
examples: GD&T datum reference frames preserved across STEP round-trip
counterexamples: IGES export loses semantic tolerance information
common_errors: Treating STEP geometry as identical across all APs
